# The test suites CI does NOT run, and the measured reason for each.
#
# This file exists because of the actual defect behind #7. 65 suites had
# stopped running without anyone deciding they should; they were not excluded,
# they were simply never named anywhere, so nothing could report them missing.
# Naming them is what makes "not run" a decision with an owner instead of an
# accident nobody can see.
#
# CI runs 162 of 169 suites, up from 92 before #13, 123 after it, and 134
# before the 2026-09-04 reconciliation. The 7 below are the remainder. Every one
# was measured against a real PostgreSQL 16 with the schema pushed,
# individually, not in a batch:
#
#   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/backenly_test \
#   TEST_DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL DIRECT_URL=$DATABASE_URL \
#   JWT_SECRET=ci-not-a-real-secret \
#   npx jest --runTestsByPath <path> --ci --forceExit
#
# "134 of 156" was true when it was written and quietly stopped being true as
# the tree grew: by 2026-09-04 twelve suites were in no manifest at all. Do not
# hand-maintain these totals. `scripts/verify-suite-accounting.ts` runs on every
# push and proves that every suite jest resolves is categorised exactly once, so
# the next drift fails CI instead of going unnoticed for months.
#
# None of them are excluded for needing a database. A database is provided by
# the `integration` and `baseline` jobs and did not fix these. Do not re-file
# them as "needs Postgres"; that was the wrong diagnosis once already.
#
# Nor are they excluded merely for FAILING. That was the old rule, and the
# reason for it was sound: `tests/core` was added on a false belief that it was
# database-free, went red on every push for weeks, and a red that is always red
# carries no information. The `baseline` job supersedes that rule for failing
# suites, by recording known failures by NAME so a suite can run while red
# without CI becoming uninformative. The 7 here are excluded for a stronger
# reason than failing: they cannot run at all, need a live model provider, or
# need an HTTP server no job starts.

# ── Cannot run at all under the current jest setup ──────────────────────────
# Both are gated on ENGINE_MODE=runtime and skip themselves otherwise. Nothing
# can satisfy that gate: jest.setup.js line 29 assigns
# ENGINE_MODE='integration' for every suite, deliberately, so that tests never
# execute real DDL. Setting ENGINE_MODE=runtime in the environment does not
# help — the setup file runs after it and overwrites it.
#
# They are dangerous rather than merely idle. jest exits 0 on a fully skipped
# suite, so both report "pass" while running one skipped test and asserting
# nothing. They were nearly added to database-free-suites.txt on exactly that
# false green. Making them run means letting tests execute real DDL, which is
# the guard jest.setup.js exists to enforce, so it is a real decision and not
# CI wiring.
__tests__/suite1.core-integration.test.ts
__tests__/suite1.real-engine-integration.test.ts

# ── Needs a live model provider ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Calls OpenAI for real. Cannot pass in CI without a key and a spend decision,
# and would be nondeterministic even then.
__tests__/lib/services/aiWorkspace.test.ts
tests/validation/master-capability-validation.test.ts

# ── Needs a running HTTP server ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Black-box suites that fetch against a live app on localhost. They need the
# Next server and the Express runtime up, which no CI job currently starts.
__tests__/security/auth-security.test.ts
__tests__/security/auth-security-fixed.test.ts
__tests__/security/oauth-security.test.ts

# ── Moved to the known-failure baseline, 2026-09-04 ─────────────────────────
# The 15 "genuine failures against a real database" that used to be listed here
# now run on the `baseline` CI job and are checked against
# tests/baseline-failures.json. They are named in .github/baseline-suites.txt.
#
# The rule this file states above ("a suite joins CI when it passes, not
# before") was the right call when the only choice was green or red. A
# name-level baseline gives a third option: run the suite, record its known
# failures by name, and go red only on a NEW one. So a failing suite can finally
# be on a blocking job without CI being permanently red and therefore ignored.
#
# Each was re-measured INDIVIDUALLY on 2026-09-04, which materially changed the
# numbers: run together they contaminate each other, and several reported more
# failures in a combined run than they actually have (deterministic-executor 5
# vs 1, monitoring 7 vs 4). The baseline records the isolated result.
